Matthew Alexander Schwartz (born October 1978) is a American attorney in private practice and currently a partner at Sullivan & Cromwell. He was been announced as a nominee to be a United States circuit judge of the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit.
Early life and education
Schwartz was born in October 1978, in New York City. He received an Artium Baccalaureus degree in 2000 from Princeton University and a Juris Doctor in 2003 from Columbia Law School. He clerked twice for Associate Justice Samuel Alito, from 2003 to 2004 when Alito was a Judge of the United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit and then from 2006 to 2007, when Alito was a Justice of the Supreme Court of the United States.
Career
Schwartz joined the white shoe law firm of Sullivan & Cromwell in New York City in 2007 as an associate and was elected partner in 2011.  He has focused mainly on securities law, mergers & acquisitions, deritive suits, antitrust law, bank regulation, contracts, constitutional law, administrative law, and general commercial litigation.
Nomination to court of appeals
On April 10, 2026, President Donald Trump announced his intention to nominate Schwartz to an unspecified seat on the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit. On April 27, 2026, Trump nominated Schwartz to the seat on the Second Circuit being vacated by Debra Ann Livingston.
Notable cases
Schwartz has served as personal counsel to President Trump in several cases, including Trump's appeal in the Stormy Daniels hush money case.
Personal life
Schwartz is married to Amy Cayne and they have one son. They reside in Scarsdale, New York.
